meta.titre: Asexual Reproduction in Fungi: spores in bread mould and budding in yeast

sections.contenu_markdown: Leave a slice of bread in a damp kitchen for a few days and a fuzzy grey or black growth appears. Add a spoonful of sugar to a bottle of warm water with a pinch of baker's yeast and the liquid begins to bubble. Both are fungi multiplying without a mate. GCE questions ask you to describe how a mould or a yeast reproduces asexually, so you must know the steps in the right order and the key word of each one.

items: Fungi have no chlorophyll, so they cannot make food by photosynthesis.
A cell has a nucleus that controls the activities of the cell.
Reproduction means producing new individuals of the same kind.

sections.titre: Asexual reproduction by spores and by budding
sections.contenu_markdown:
### What a fungus is
Fungi have no chlorophyll. They feed on dead or living organic matter. Bread mould is made of fine threads called **hyphae**, which together form a **mycelium**. It releases enzymes onto its food, digests it outside the body and absorbs the soluble products. Yeast is different because it is a **single cell**.

### Asexual reproduction
In asexual reproduction **one parent** produces new individuals. There are no gametes and no fertilisation. The offspring are genetically identical to the parent. It is fast and needs no partner, but it produces no variation.

### Spore formation in bread mould
1. Upright hyphae called **sporangiophores** grow up from the mycelium.
2. The tip of each one swells into a round **sporangium**, which fills with many tiny **spores**.
3. When the sporangium is ripe and dry its wall breaks open and the spores are released.
4. The spores are very light and are carried by air currents.
5. A spore that lands on moist, warm food **germinates**. It grows hyphae and forms a new mycelium.

### Budding in yeast
1. A small bump, the **bud**, forms on the side of the parent cell.
2. The nucleus of the parent divides and one daughter nucleus moves into the bud.
3. The bud grows larger and is cut off from the parent by a narrow neck.
4. The bud separates and becomes a new yeast cell, which can form its own buds. Sometimes the buds stay joined and form a short chain.

| Feature | Bread mould | Yeast |
|---|---|---|
| Body | Mycelium of hyphae | One oval cell |
| Asexual method | Spores made in sporangia | Budding |
| Spread | Spores carried by air | Buds break off in the liquid food |

variantes.quand_utiliser: When a question carries several marks
variantes.contenu_markdown: Count about one mark for each separate point. Write the points in the order in which they happen, and use the exact terms: hyphae, sporangiophore, sporangium, spores, germinate, bud. Name the organism and the word 'asexual' at the start, for example 'Bread mould reproduces asexually by spores.'

variantes.quand_utiliser: When a question asks for advantages of this method
variantes.contenu_markdown: Spores are made in very large numbers, so some will reach suitable food. They are tiny and light, so wind carries them far. They are produced by one parent, so no partner is needed, and a new colony is made quickly.

variantes.quand_utiliser: When a question asks about mould on food or about yeast in fermentation
variantes.contenu_markdown: Fungi grow fastest in **warm**, **moist** surroundings with a **supply of organic food**. A cold place slows growth. Dry food stops growth because spores need water to germinate. Yeast feeding on sugar without oxygen makes alcohol and carbon dioxide, which is why it is used to make dough rise.

sections.enonce_markdown: With the help of a labelled sequence of steps in words, describe how yeast reproduces asexually. (4 marks)

etapes.action: Read the command word and the organism.
etapes.justification: 'Describe' asks for what happens, in order. The organism is yeast, so the method is budding.
etapes.resultat_markdown: Answer about budding in a single yeast cell.

etapes.action: Start with the first visible change.
etapes.justification: Examiners give a mark for each distinct stage, so each stage needs its own sentence.
etapes.resultat_markdown: A small bud grows out from the side of the parent cell.

etapes.action: Add the part played by the nucleus.
etapes.justification: A new cell must receive a nucleus, so the nucleus divides and one copy moves into the bud.
etapes.resultat_markdown: One daughter nucleus enters the bud.

etapes.action: Finish with the separation and what it means.
etapes.justification: The last mark is for the new individual and for its genetic identity.
etapes.resultat_markdown: The bud is cut off, becomes a new cell identical to the parent, and can bud again.

sections.conclusion_markdown: Yeast reproduces asexually by **budding**. A small bud grows out of the parent cell. The nucleus divides and one daughter nucleus moves into the bud. The bud enlarges, is cut off by a narrow neck and separates as a new yeast cell that is **genetically identical** to the parent.

items.pourquoi_faux: A seed is made by flowering plants after sexual reproduction. Moulds make spores, which are single cells made by one parent.
items.correction_markdown: Bread mould reproduces by spores released from sporangia.

items.erreur_markdown: Yeast cells fuse together to make a bud.
items.pourquoi_faux: Fusion of cells belongs to sexual reproduction. In budding there is only one parent.
items.correction_markdown: A bud grows out of one parent cell, receives a nucleus and separates.

items.erreur_markdown: Asexual reproduction gives offspring that are different from the parent.
items.pourquoi_faux: With one parent and no mixing of gametes, the offspring carry the same genes as the parent.
items.correction_markdown: Asexual offspring are genetically identical to the parent; variation comes from sexual reproduction.

items.erreur_markdown: A mould is a plant because it grows on bread.
items.pourquoi_faux: Moulds have no chlorophyll and no true roots, stems or leaves, and they cannot make food. They feed on organic matter.
items.correction_markdown: A mould is a fungus that feeds on dead or decaying material.

items.erreur_markdown: Spores are the gametes of a fungus.
items.pourquoi_faux: Gametes fuse, but the spores described here grow directly into a new mycelium without fusing.
items.correction_markdown: Spores are asexual reproductive cells that germinate on their own.

items.enonce_markdown:
Complete each blank with the correct term.

(a) The mass of threads that makes up the body of a mould is called a ______.
(b) The round structure at the top of an upright hypha that holds the spores is a ______.
(c) A yeast cell makes new cells by a process called ______.
(d) Asexual offspring are ______ to the parent.

A laboratory starts with 50 yeast cells in a warm sugar solution. Suppose the number of cells doubles every 2 hours because every cell makes one bud that separates.

(a) How many cells are present after 6 hours?
(b) After how many hours does the number first pass 1000?
(c) A mould colony has 40 sporangia and each releases 500 spores. How many spores are released? If only 1 spore in every 1000 lands on suitable food and germinates, how many new colonies start?
items.solution_markdown:
(a) 6 hours is 3 doublings: 50 x 2 x 2 x 2 = **400 cells**.
(b) Counts at 2-hour steps: 50, 100, 200, 400, 800, 1600. The first value above 1000 is 1600, at 10 hours: **10 hours**.
(c) 40 x 500 = **20000 spores**. One in 1000 germinates: 20000 / 1000 = **20 new colonies**.

items.enonce_markdown:
A student places three slices of fresh bread in clear bags. Slice A is moist and kept in a warm room. Slice B is kept dry in a warm room. Slice C is moist and kept in a refrigerator. After one week one slice is covered in mould.

(a) Which slice will have the most mould? Explain.
(b) Why are slices B and C almost free of mould?
(c) State two advantages and one disadvantage of reproduction by spores.
items.solution_markdown:
(a) **Slice A**. Spores already present on the bread had water, warmth and food, so they germinated and the hyphae spread.
(b) Slice B has no water, which spores need to germinate. In slice C the low temperature slows the activities of the fungus so growth is very slow.
(c) Advantages (any two): very large numbers of spores are made; light spores are spread widely by air; no partner is needed so colonies form quickly. Disadvantage: the offspring are identical to the parent, so there is no variation to help the species when conditions change.

items_markdown: Bread mould reproduces asexually by spores made in sporangia on upright hyphae.
Yeast, a single-celled fungus, reproduces asexually by budding.
One parent, no gametes and no fertilisation means the offspring are genetically identical.
Spores need water, warmth and food to germinate into a new mycelium.
For a describe question, give the stages in order with the correct key terms.
